# Proof route and fidelity

The final cubic statements and their encodings are unchanged; all six frozen
SHA256 hashes match the supplied specification. The supplied Cook–Levin file
is preserved verbatim after line-ending normalization. It is used solely as
an explicit theorem parameter. No defect in the paper or frozen definitions
is asserted by this development.

The proved reduction uses an alternative construction for Berger–Leighton's
Section 3.2 (conference paper, pp. 32–38). It proves the same final problems
on the same cubic lattice, rather than reproducing the literal Figure 3 word
or claiming a line-by-line formalisation of Lemmas 3.3–3.8. This is the proof
method change authorized by the user.

The source chain goes directly from arbitrary binary-variable CNF to balanced
three-dimensional matching, then to four-item numerical bins and positive-even
unary modified packing. Radix magnitudes are polynomially bounded, so emitting
unary fields is a genuine polynomial-time reduction. Typed gadget vertices
are relabelled by a proved equivalence; dummy items are emitted in vertex
order with a proved permutation equivalence. Existing earlier maps are retained.

The cubic frame uses two opposite square perimeters and their joining edge,
a saturated skeleton, modular anchor counts, straight wall crossings,
positive-even rectangular item strips, and distinct-depth exterior routes.
Exact routing parity allows precisely the literal number of inserted P
residues. Every H and P position is included in the full self-avoiding walk.
The soundness proof permits arbitrary item shapes; rectangles are a choice
only in the constructive direction. Finite coordinate examples are supplementary
checks, not hypotheses or substitutes for the general proofs.

Theorem 3.2 (p. 32) is proved independently using the geometric edge-count
bound and its equality case, including side zero. Both NP-membership results
from the observation in footnote 1 (p. 31) have actual polynomial-time verifier
machines. The three final complexity theorems require exactly the explicit
Cook–Levin hypothesis; the geometric theorem and membership proofs require none.
